editorial:
Imagine having your whole life planned out, only to realize you forgot one tiny detail: you actually failed a class. That is exactly where you find Levi, a star tennis player who is headed for a great university scholarship. The problem is he didn't actually graduate high school, and he has to keep it a secret from his parents. You will love the awkward energy of summer school, where Levi meets a group of misfits and a cute girl who helps him see that life is about more than just getting an A. It is a lighthearted ride that feels like a warm summer day, mixing high school stress with some really funny moments.

What really works here is the chemistry between the leads and the relatable panic of trying to hide a huge mistake. The pacing is quick, though some of the jokes feel a bit dated. If you enjoy coming-of-age stories with a lot of heart, you should definitely give this one a shot. It is a great pick for a lazy weekend afternoon.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when Levi finally stops lying to his parents and admits he failed. Instead of being totally disappointed, they support him. He finishes his summer coursework and learns that being a good person is more important than a perfect transcript. He ends up staying with the girl he fell for, proving that his failure actually led him to a much happier and more honest life.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves cute high school romances and underdog stories.
